Sloooow. Maybe more bar than restaurant.
Feb 2020
Did think that this was a simpler alternative to tracking down and choosing between different HCMC places when I can't tell the difference. Unadventurous approach to opt for Western food I know, so shoot me. The staff seemed to be very focused on providing us with beers and wine when we just wanted a couple of soft drinks and a prompt meal. My burger (which was fine) took around 25 minutes. My wife's pizza took nearly 45 minutes and that came about as a result of a couple of reminders. 

We were the only people getting foor at the point when we ordered so I'm baffled at the slow speed. Maybe later, when it's a happening lively bar serving customers who want that third beer before the meal arrives, it'll get its act together.

Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam206 contributions

Hidden Music Gem
Jul 2019 • Friends
The pizza is reasonably pleasant, great happy hour deals and the staff are the most friendly, welcoming staff in Vietnam if not anywhere! It is not just a tokenistic welcome, key staff circulate all if the tables throughout the night - chatting, joining you for a drink, checking you're enjoying yourself etc. The band on a Saturday night is phenomenal - best band in Ho Chi Minh since the Indonesian band left Hard Rock Cafe a few months ago to go to Hong Kong. The atmosphere is electric, fantastic vibe and everyone throwing themselves into the mood. Hard to beat Dailo's on a Saturday night.

Good little spot
Aug 2018
If you're looking for a Bui Vien ex-pat bar this isn't it. This place has a nice pool table, fantastic staff, and pretty good food. The Thursday night we visited there was great live band karaoke. It's hard to get to, down a dark side street and up a flight of stairs but worth the visit. Huan the manager, and Patrick the owner, are extremely kind and welcoming. Take a chance if you're nearby and want a break from the loud club scene of the ex-pat bars.

Love the food
Nov 2016 • Friends
My Boss introduced us to this bar, which is a bit out of the way from the usual bars here in Vietnam. Its at the end of thai van lung street and is on the second floor of an old 2 storey establishment. We didnt expect much on the food as the crowd their usually drinks beer/liquors and just playing billiards and darts. But after looking at the menu and ordering some Singaporean dishes like hokkien mee, laksa, and other appetizers like buttered clams and asparagus wrapped in bacon, i will surely come back and recommend the place because the food was delicious and service was fast as well.
